text:
A: Hello? Oh, hello, can you hear me? Sorry, I keep leaning into the screen.
B: Yeah. Alright. I'm Craig.
A: Julie. Hello, Craig. Have you had a good day?
B: Yeah, not bad. Bit long. Work, then this.
A: Oh, same. I was on an early. What is it you do, if you don't mind me asking?
B: Quality inspection. Engineering. Measuring parts.
A: Measuring parts. Oh, right. For cars, or...?
B: Er, all sorts. Aluminium bits, for other firms. Some go into car stuff, yeah.
A: My son would like that. He's a forklift driver, at one of the warehouses, but he's mad on cars. He's always on about some engine or other and I just nod. Sorry, I don't know anything about it.
B: That's alright. What's he drive?
A: Erm, it's a Golf, I think? A black one. He's always washing it on the drive and leaving the bucket out.
B: Golf's a good car. Sensible. I've got an A3, same sort of thing underneath.
A: Oh, is it? There you go, I've learned something. Where are you, Craig?
B: Swindon.
A: Oh, Swindon, I've been through there, there's that magic roundabout, isn't there? I went round it twice and came out the wrong way.
B: [laughs] Yeah, everyone does. The roadworks on the A419 are worse, to be fair. Doing my head in.
A: Oh, I can imagine. We've got the same in Basingstoke, they dig a road up, fill it in, then dig it up again a week later. Do you live on your own, or...?
B: Er, with my mum and dad at the moment. Saving for a deposit.
A: Oh, well, that's very sensible. My Liam's still with me at twenty-eight, him and his girlfriend. I don't mind, really, it's nice having the house full. Does your mum still cook for you?
B: Yeah. Most nights. She keeps putting extra veg on my plate.
A: [laughs] Good for her! I do exactly the same. I hide it in the shepherd's pie, carrots and that, he doesn't even notice.
B: Yeah, mine does that with the chilli. I've noticed.
A: [laughs] Oh dear. Well, she means well.
B: Yeah. I've been helping out more, to be fair. My dad's knees are going, so I do the bins, the garden, that sort of thing.
A: Oh, that's good of you. That's really good. I work with older people, I'm in a care home, and the ones whose families do the little things, it makes all the difference, you know. Has he seen anyone about the knees?
B: Er, he's on a list. Physio, I think.
A: Make sure he keeps moving, even just a little walk. That's what they always tell our lot. Sorry, I'm going into work mode.
B: No, that's alright. That's useful, yeah.
A: Have you got any holidays planned? Something to look forward to?
B: Thinking Tenerife again. September. Been three times, same place.
A: Oh, I don't blame you, if you know it. I'm terrible with flying, I check the passports about ten times before we even leave the—
